---
title: Formatting
---

`biblint format` writes a canonical representation of the BibTeX it understands.
By default it changes layout, entry-type spelling, and field-name spelling only.

## Default shape

Input:

```bibtex
@ARTICLE{Smith2024,
author={Smith, John},
title={A Study},
year=2024
}
```

Default output:

```bibtex
@article{Smith2024,
  author = {Smith, John},
  title = {A Study},
  year = 2024
}
```

The default does not align equals signs, sort entries or fields, add braces, change values, or remove duplicate and empty fields.
It separates entries with a blank line.

## Layout and ordering

```toml
[format]
indent = 2                 # a space count, or "tab"
align = false              # or a field-name column number
blank-lines = true
trailing-commas = true
wrap = 80                  # false disables wrapping
sort = ["key"]
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]
```

`align = false` disables alignment.
`sort = true` uses key order, and `sort-fields = true` uses biblint's built-in field order.
Lists provide an explicit order.

## Value transforms

These settings are opt-in because they alter value spelling or representation:

| Setting     | Effect                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `curly`         | Enclose values in braces.                                  |
| `numeric`         | Render numeric values as bare literals.                    |
| `months`         | Normalize recognized month names.                          |
| `format-page-ranges`        | Normalize page ranges.                                     |
| `escape` / `unescape` | Convert supported text between Unicode and LaTeX.          |
| `encode-urls`        | Encode URL underscores.                                    |
| `strip-enclosing-braces`        | Remove one outer brace group.                              |
| `enclosing-braces` / `remove-braces` | Select fields whose brace depth changes.                   |
| `drop-all-caps`        | Convert all-caps values to title case.                     |
| `wrap`        | Wrap long values at a configured width.                    |
| `lowercase`        | Lowercase entry types and field names. Enabled by default. |

The escape table is package-independent.
Unconvertible characters are preserved and reported by `unsupported_escape`.

## Cleanup and semantic transforms

```toml
[format]
remove-empty-fields = true
remove-duplicate-fields = true
omit = ["abstract"]
strip-comments = true
tidy-comments = true
max-authors = 3
generate-keys = true
duplicate-kinds = ["doi", "citation"]
merge = "combine"
```

These settings can remove information, change author lists, generate keys, or merge entries.
`merge` accepts `first`, `last`, `combine`, and `overwrite`.
By default it considers DOI, citation, and abstract duplicates.
Add `key` to `duplicate-kinds` to include key duplicates.

`generate-keys` uses the same formula evaluator as the `key_format` rule.
See [Citekey generation](key-generation.md) for a Better BibTeX syntax subset.

## Fix safety

`check --format --fix` applies safe formatting edits when formatting is explicitly enabled.
For a formatting-only policy check, use `biblint format references.bib --check`.
Transforms that can change content or identity require:

```console
biblint check references.bib --format --fix --unsafe-fixes
```

The standalone `format` command applies the configured profile directly.

## Preserved source

Comments, special entries, and unstructured source are retained unless a configured transform targets them.
Unstructured source is reported as `unsupported_construct` rather than discarded.
